title.value: On Dynamic Programming Decompositions of Static Risk Measures in Markov Decision Processes
title.justification: The title accurately reflects the main subject of the paper, which discusses dynamic programming decompositions in the context of Markov Decision Processes with a focus on static risk measures.
title.quote: On Dynamic Programming Decompositions of Static Risk Measures in Markov Decision Processes

extractions.description: The paper critiques the existing dynamic programming decompositions used in Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) for optimizing static risk-averse objectives, especially those involving risk measures like Conditional-Value-at-Risk (CVaR) and Entropic-Value-at-Risk (EVaR). It highlights the suboptimality of these decompositions and contrasts them with Value-at-Risk (VaR), providing new insights and corrections to previous approaches.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The primary focus of the paper is on the theoretical aspects and corrections of dynamic programming approaches in risk-averse reinforcement learning, rather than directly addressing climate or ecological sustainable development goals.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Risk-averse reinforcement learning (RL) seeks to provide a risk-averse policy for high-stakes real-world decision problems. These high-stake domains include autonomous driving, robot collision avoidance, liver transplant timing, HIV treatment, unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV), and investment liquidation.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not focus on a specific category related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development. It primarily addresses theoretical issues in reinforcement learning algorithms concerning risk measures.
primary_category.quote: Our findings are significant because practitioners who make risk-averse decisions in high-stakes scenarios need to have confidence in the correctness of the algorithms they use.

secondary_categories.justification: There is no secondary focus on climate or ecological sustainable development. The paper primarily discusses risk management in reinforcement learning without direct application to the provided sustainability categories.
secondary_categories.quote: The work raises awareness that popular static CVaR and EVaR MDP algorithms are suboptimal, and their analyses are inaccurate.

primary_sub_category.justification: The focus is on theoretical corrections to risk measure algorithms in MDPs rather than any applied sub-category under Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
primary_sub_category.quote: We also prove that a similar decomposition approach is optimal for policy optimization and evaluation when solving MDPs with the VaR objective.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The paper remains theoretical and focused on algorithmic issues in MDPs rather than any application in sustainable development.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Our results also affect applications of these algorithms, such as automated vehicle motion planning.

applications.justification: Though mentioned as an application, the paper's primary interest is in the theoretical foundations rather than the application itself in automated vehicles.
applications.quote: Our results also affect applications of these algorithms, such as automated vehicle motion planning.
